📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough shep-client adds shared dog identity, startup, runtime, request, stop, and error APIs. shep-core defines shared dog-name and exit-code constants. shep-cli updates dog integrations to use these APIs and adds feature-gated schema testing helpers. ### Changes **Shared dog lifecycle** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Shared errors and exit codes**
`crates/shep-core/src/{exit.rs,protocol/request/envelope.rs}`, `crates/shep-client/src/{client.rs,connection.rs,spawn.rs,reconnect/link_state.rs,dogs/error.rs}`, `crates/shep-cli/src/exit.rs`|shep-core defines shared exit-code constants. Client, connection, spawn, link, and shepherd errors map to those codes. shep-cli converts shared codes to its ExitCode variants.| |**Dog identity and startup APIs**
`crates/shep-core/src/{dogs.rs,paths.rs}`, `crates/shep-client/src/{dogs/identity.rs,dogs/startup.rs,reconnect/reconnecting.rs}`|DogIdentity supplies handshake and config-section names. Startup helpers parse arguments and resolve home paths. ReconnectingClient adds `connect_as`.| |**Typed requests and dog runtime**
`crates/shep-client/src/{typed.rs,dogs/*,client.rs,lib.rs,reconnect/reconnecting.rs}`, `crates/shep-core/src/protocol/request/*`, `crates/shep-cli/src/dog/runtime.rs`, `crates/shep-client/Cargo.toml`, `docs/dogs.md`|shep-client adds typed request methods, DogRuntime, and section parsing. Unexpected replies identify request and response variants. Section parse errors report the section and line without retaining source text. The CLI-local runtime module is removed.| |**Stop tokens and signal listeners**
`crates/shep-client/src/dogs/{stop.rs,mod.rs}`, `crates/shep-client/Cargo.toml`|The watch-backed Stop API supports stop requests, waiting, sleeping, and signal listeners. Dog module documentation describes startup and stopping.| |**shep-cli dog integration**
`crates/shep-cli/src/{adopted.rs,commands/dogs/vet/mod.rs,dog/*}`, `crates/shep-daemon/src/dogs/spec.rs`|bark and metrics use the shared runtime, typed requests, and Stop API. Dog-name environment setup uses DOG_NAME_VAR, and dog configuration errors include parse details.| **Schema testing helpers** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Schema and printed-key helpers**
`crates/shep-client/src/testing/*`|Feature-gated helpers return sorted schema property names and extract setting keys from printed configuration text. Tests cover renamed keys, prose, and stale keys.| **Priority:** ➖ Normal **Estimated code review effort:** 4 (Complex) | ~45 minutes ### Sequence Diagram(s) ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant OS as OS signal participant Listener as Stop signal listener participant Stop as Stop watch channel participant Bark as bark event loop OS->>Listener: deliver SIGINT or SIGTERM Listener->>Stop: set stop requested Stop->>Bark: resolve stop.wait() Bark->>Bark: return ExitCode::Success ```
**Merge Risk:** _⚪ Minimal_ · up to `385f9` No confirmed issue blocks merge; spawn failures retain their previous exit codes. ### Security Architecture Review **Security architecture risk:** _🟡 Moderate_ · up to `385f9` Shared dog APIs now affect multiple integrations. No new authorization bypass was established, but interrupted shutdown behavior and some deployment controls remain uncertain. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details **Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The relevant identity exposure is to clients able to reach the daemon socket, not to a newly added network entrypoint. Socket-level access restrictions were not established by the inspected evidence. **Security Findings and Attack Paths** - _observed_ — The daemon does not bind a requested DogConfig section to the handshake name in the inspected dispatch path. An arbitrary-name handshake and named section request were already available through existing public client APIs, so this PR was not shown to introduce that capability. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — The inspected daemon handshake checks protocol compatibility, but does not authenticate the asserted dog name against a peer identity. This behavior predates the new identity wrapper. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _inferred_ — A stop requested during bark resubscription may wait for that operation and reconciliation before the loop exits and drops its subscription. The previous signal-selection path was likewise outside those awaits, so a worsened shutdown guarantee was not established. **Hardening Proposals** - _proposed_ — If dog configurations require isolation, authenticate socket clients and bind section requests to the authenticated identity; the current name is an assertion, not that control. - _proposed_ — Define whether Stop must interrupt an in-progress handover, then exercise stop-versus-resubscription ordering and subscription cleanup against that contract.

Full details: Linked Issues check **Explanation** The PR implements the shared dog APIs in `#613`, including stop handling, typed requests, identity and reconnect behavior, runtime and section parsing, shared errors and exit codes, startup helpers, path helpers, and schema-test helpers. Tests cover shared SIGINT/SIGTERM behavior and the new APIs. The supplied evidence does not show the required log-rotate regression test that asserts supervised `SIGTERM` exits with code 0 instead of 15. The summary also states that external dog migrations were not tested.
